title: Normalize shifts of the explicit common-field adjunction
statement: Fix a prime l, an algebraic closure Ω of Padic l, a finite-field datum D with l ≠ D.p, finite-type quasi-compact D.k-schemes X and Y, and a separated finite-type quasi-compact D.k-morphism f : X → Y. Let A be RingStageAssembly l Ω D hl for f [def-sf-ring-stage-assembly-data], and P a RationalStageAssembly over A [lem-sf-rational-stage-localization]. No absolute separatedness is assumed. Let L_c, R_c and a_c be the explicit rationalCommonLeft.functor, rationalCommonRight.functor and rationalCommonAdjunction [lem-sf-rational-common-scalar-coherence]. There exist integer CommShift structures on the endpoint common-field inclusion functors, chosen independently of c, and on L_c and R_c, such that L_c and R_c are triangulated, the actual unit and counit of a_c commute with shifts, and the inverse canonical stage-restriction isomorphisms for L_c and R_c commute with shifts using the original P.operation shifts. This is Nonempty RationalCommonShiftData. No functor, adjunction, comparison map or transition equation is an existential output.

source.place: Construction 6.6, common-field descent step 4 only: endpoint shift normalization and exactness after explicit unshifted descent.

proof.text: At each finite coefficient field, use the canonical integral rationalization shift. Rationalization is a localization by residue Tor. Localize the integral left-operation shift along the actual localization comparison q, obtaining a normalized rational left shift with q commuting with shifts. Exactness follows from exact rationalization, arrow essential surjectivity, integral exactness, and the precomposition-isomorphism criterion.

Apply the finite normalized scalar-shift square to this family and sfLocalizationShiftDescent to obtain the actual common-field left shift. Every distinguished triangle is isomorphic to an included finite-stage distinguished triangle; finite normalized exactness and canonical inclusion exactness make the left operation exact. No separate exact-adjunction-descent datum is used.

Correct a canonical endpoint inclusion shift by localizing its composite with canonical rationalization, now using the supplied rationalization shift. The localization comparison equation computes this corrected shift on every integral representative. A generic naturality calculation using the old and normalized q shift squares shows that the inverse stage restriction commutes with the supplied finite left shift and these corrected inclusion shifts. P.shiftX and P.shiftY allow the correction to be evaluated at one compactification, so it is independent of c. Residue Tor gives literal integral representatives of all rational objects. If there is no compactification the family-indexed fields are vacuous.

Give the actual right adjoint the right-adjoint shift of the common left shift. The triangulated-adjunction theorem proves right exactness and the adjunction shift theorem proves the actual unit and counit squares. Apply the proved generic mate-shift lemma to the finite adjunction, the common adjunction, and the two inverse stage restrictions. The descended counit component equation proves its hypothesis, yielding bShift with the supplied finite right shift. These constructions give every field of RationalCommonShiftData.
